altstadt: Zurich's old town on the right bank of the Limmat: narrow lanes with colourful houses, shops, bars and little squares, and the Limmatquai along the river with the old guild houses. Take your time: it's almost all pedestrian.
grossmunster: The great Romanesque church with twin towers, the symbol of Zurich and the place where Zwingli began the Swiss Reformation. You can climb the Karlsturm, the right-hand tower, to see the rooftops, the river and the lake.
fraumunster: The church with two slender spires opposite the Grossmünster, famous for the five stained-glass windows of the choir and the transept rose window painted by Marc Chagall in 1970, alongside windows by Augusto Giacometti. Next door is the cloister with its frescoes.
lindenhof: A tree-lined terrace on the hill of the first Roman settlement, above the Limmat, with a fountain, the old giant chess game and one of the finest views of the river and the two church towers.
bahnhofstrasse: Zurich's most elegant and expensive street, 1.4 kilometres from the station to the lake: windows of watches and jewellery, the banks, the trams and, on Paradeplatz, the Confiserie Sprüngli. You can walk it in a quarter of an hour, but you'll stop a lot.
landesmuseum: The museum of Swiss history, in a neo-Gothic castle next to the station: armour, stained glass, original rooms from the Middle Ages on and an exhibition on the country's history ("History of Switzerland"). It also has a park and a bistro.
kunsthaus: Switzerland's most important art museum: Giacometti, Munch, Monet, Van Gogh, Picasso, Chagall and a large modern art collection, with a room devoted to Swiss painters. David Chipperfield's new building hosts the temporary exhibitions.
lago: Lake Zurich, with the promenade from Bürkliplatz towards Bellevue and Zürichhorn: plane trees, benches, sailing boats and, on clear days, the Alps in the background. Boats for lake trips leave from Bürkliplatz.
poly: The 1889 funicular that climbs from Central to the terrace of the Federal Institute of Technology (ETH): from up there you get the best view of the old town, with the Limmat, the rooftops and the towers of the Grossmünster.
uetliberg: Zurich's mountain, at 870 metres: a train gets you there in about 20 minutes from the main station, and the summit is a ten-minute walk away. From the lookout tower you see the city, the lake and, in good weather, the Alps.
lindt: Lindt's chocolate museum, on the lake south of Zurich: from the history of cocoa to production, with a huge chocolate fountain and a shop with free tastings on every floor. Get there by train or by boat.
